title: Expected and actual results
summary: A test compares an expected result with the actual result. A passing test only checks the case you gave it.
introduction: A test compares an expected result with the actual result. A passing test only checks the case you gave it. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A test compares an expected result with the actual result. A passing test only checks the case you gave it.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: The JavaScript examples run in this browser. The text examples are test plans you can work through on paper.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Software Testing. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
console.log(add(2, 3) === 5);
blocks.title: Expected and actual results

blocks.text: The result is true: the actual answer matches 5. This does not prove every possible input works.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Try adding zero and write the expected answer first.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: One passing example is not proof that a whole program has no bugs.
For more detail later, use this [Software Testing further reading](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Extensions/Testing).
